name: Negotiate investment legal agreements
summary: Four investment counsel and two paralegals negotiate the agreements behind the model manager's investments: co-investment and direct deal documents, fund partnership agreements and side letters, external manager agreements, ISDA and clearing agreements, and a steady flow of amendments, consents and waivers. Counsel checks each instruction against the committee approval and the client IMAs, marks up the other side's paper, gets business, tax, compliance or risk input, and negotiates over one to three rounds before two officers sign and key terms go into a tracker. Most elapsed time is waiting on the other side and on internal reviewers; outside law firms are used on about a third of matters.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with a six-person legal services team inside legal and compliance, using outside firms on large deals.
baseline.notes: Word documents and redlines by email, a document management system, a spreadsheet term tracker and electronic signature; no contract lifecycle management system assumed.

trigger: An investment team, the manager research team, treasury or a counterparty's counsel sends a request for legal documentation: a term sheet, draft agreement, amendment or consent request.
end_state: The agreement is executed by both sides, its key terms are recorded and it is handed to the team that closes or onboards the investment, manager or counterparty; or the negotiation is abandoned.

volume.seasonality: Busier in the fourth quarter and before fund final closings.

evidence.note: About 35 direct and co-investment transactions and 15 fund commitments a year (mgr_nr21 and the organisation file), plus manager, counterparty agreements and amendments; the monthly range is the process map's tier C estimate.

About 18 hours of counsel time per agreement at 14 agreements a month is about 1.9 FTE of the four counsel. Loaded cost from the organisation file, above the Job Bank median for NOC 41101 because investment counsel are senior lawyers.
Matter opening, execution versions, signature packets and the term tracker; loaded cost from the organisation file.
Triage, outside counsel decisions, non-standard positions and signature; the General Counsel sits on the Management Investment Committee (mgr_ar21).
Stands in for the private equity, real estate, infrastructure and credit principals who settle business points on deal, fund and consent documents.

steps.name: Log the request and open the legal matter
steps.description: The paralegal logs the legal instruction in the matter tracker, opens a matter folder in the document system, attaches the term sheet, approval and the counterparty's draft if any, and pulls the precedent agreements and side letters held with the same general partner, manager or dealer.

error.defect_description: Wrong precedent or superseded side letter attached.

next.condition: fund partnership agreement and side letter already negotiated under the commitment

evidence.note: Matter intake is common in-house practice; the 10% share of fund commitments whose terms were negotiated in fund-commitment follows the trigger shares.

steps.name: Triage the matter and decide on outside counsel
steps.description: The general counsel reviews the new matters each day or two, assigns an investment counsel by asset class and workload, and decides whether outside counsel is needed for size, foreign law, tax structuring or a tight deadline.

evidence.note: Outside firms are used on large deals per the organisation file's process description; the 30% share is tier C.

steps.name: Engage outside counsel
steps.description: Investment counsel instructs the outside law firm with the scope, approved terms, key positions and deadline, asks for a fee estimate, and has the engagement letter and estimate approved under the procurement and outside counsel guidelines.

control.basis: Procurement policy and outside counsel guidelines: approved engagement and fee estimate before work starts

evidence.note: Engagement letters and fee estimates are common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Check the instruction against the approval and set positions
steps.description: Counsel compares the instruction with the committee approval or term sheet, checks the client IMA permits the investment and that the model manager signs as agent, and sets the negotiating positions from the playbook: confidentiality carve-outs for clients and regulators, liability limited to client assets, tax, reporting and most favoured nation rights.

control.basis: OSC exemption order for the model manager: policies preventing investments that contravene the restrictions in each member's IMA

evidence.note: Investments must stay within the restrictions in each member's IMA (osc_mgr_2017); limited partner positions on fiduciary duty, exculpation and indemnification (ilpa_gov). Times tier C.

steps.name: Counterparty or outside counsel provides the draft
steps.description: Most agreements start on the other side's paper: the general partner's partnership agreement, the sponsor's co-investment agreement, the manager's agreement or the dealer's ISDA schedule. For the model manager-form documents, outside counsel or the other side returns a first mark-up.

evidence.note: Timing after first review depends on the other party's response time; the one to ten day wait is tier C.

steps.name: Review the draft and prepare the mark-up and issues list
steps.description: Counsel, or outside counsel with in-house review, reads the draft clause by clause against the position list and precedents, marks it up and writes an issues list that separates legal points from business points for the investment team.

error.defect_description: A non-standard clause (indemnity, confidentiality, governing law) is missed.

evidence.note: Model documents and ILPA positions are used as reference; mix of agreements and times tier C.

steps.name: Deal team settles the business points
steps.description: The principal on the deal or fund reviews the issues list, decides on fees, governance rights, key person, transfer and exit terms, and tells counsel which points to press, trade or concede, often after a call with the managing director.

evidence.note: Deal teams own business terms; consents such as GP-led transactions need the investor to evaluate terms and elect (ilpa_gpled). The principal stands in for all private market teams. Times tier C.

steps.name: Portfolio manager settles the manager agreement terms
steps.description: The portfolio manager who owns the mandate confirms the investment guidelines, benchmark, fee schedule, reporting and termination terms in the manager's agreement match what the committee approved and the manager offered in the search.

evidence.note: Portfolio managers own mandate terms; pm_global_credit stands in for public equity and alternatives portfolio managers. Times tier C.

steps.name: Total portfolio management settles derivative agreement terms
steps.description: The total portfolio manager reviews the ISDA schedule, credit support annex or clearing agreement terms that affect trading: eligible products, termination events, collateral thresholds, minimum transfer amounts and eligible collateral, and agrees positions with counsel.

evidence.note: Initial margin rules phased in from September 2021 and 2022 for groups above $75 billion and $12 billion of notional and require agreed methodology, custody and netting documentation. Times tier C.

steps.name: Tax review of the provisions
steps.description: The tax manager reviews withholding, tax status representations, structure and treaty positions, FATCA and CRS clauses and any tax indemnity, and returns comments or confirms the drafting protects each client's tax-exempt status.

control.basis: Tax sign-off on tax provisions of investment agreements

evidence.note: Tax review of investment documents is common practice for tax-exempt public pension investors; times tier C.

steps.name: Compliance checks the investment guidelines
steps.description: A compliance analyst checks that each guideline in the manager agreement is clear enough to code in the compliance engine and is consistent with the restrictions in the client IMA and pool documents, and suggests drafting fixes.

control.basis: OSC exemption order for the model manager: compliance system covering IMA restrictions and sub-adviser monitoring

evidence.note: Restrictions set out in the IMAs must be prevented from being contravened, including by sub-advisers; times tier C.

steps.name: Risk reviews counterparty credit and collateral terms
steps.description: The investment risk manager checks the counterparty's approved credit limit, the collateral thresholds, eligible collateral and haircuts, termination triggers and netting opinion coverage, and confirms or requests changes.
inputs: ISDA schedule and credit support terms

control.basis: Counterparty credit policy: risk approval of credit terms before trading

evidence.note: Netting requires written contracts with legal review; margin terms agreed before trading. Times tier C.

steps.name: Send the mark-up to the other side
steps.description: Counsel consolidates the business, tax, compliance and risk comments into one mark-up and covering issues list and sends it to the counterparty's counsel, proposing a call for the open points.

evidence.note: Common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for the counterparty's response
steps.description: The general partner, sponsor, manager or dealer reviews the mark-up with its counsel; general partners collect comments from many limited partners before replying, and dealers queue documentation behind other clients.

evidence.note: Turnaround depends on the other party; two to fourteen day waits are tier C.

steps.name: Review the response and negotiate open points
steps.description: Counsel reviews the counterparty's response, holds a negotiation call, updates the issues list, checks business concessions with the investment team by email and either agrees the text, sends another turn or escalates a non-standard position.

error.defect_description: Concession recorded inconsistently across the agreement and side letter.

evidence.note: Negotiated agreements take one to four months depending on risk; median 40 days from negotiation to signature for supplier contracts. The number of rounds (about 1.7 on average) is tier C.

steps.name: General counsel decides on a non-standard position
steps.description: The general counsel reviews a point the counterparty will not move on, such as uncapped indemnities, foreign governing law, waiver of public body protections or weak confidentiality, and accepts the risk, proposes a compromise or instructs counsel to hold firm.

control.basis: Legal department escalation: general counsel approval of deviations from standard positions

next.condition: compromise or firm position sent back

evidence.note: Terms limited partners are urged to reject; escalation practice and rates tier C.

steps.name: Confirm the final terms are within the approval and mandates
steps.description: Counsel checks the agreed text against the committee approval, the client IMAs and pool documents and the conditions attached to the approval, and confirms the signing structure and authorised signatories.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy: execution within approved terms

evidence.note: Approval authorities are defined and IMA restrictions bind; the 6% re-approval rate is tier C.

steps.name: Committee re-approves a material change
steps.description: The investment team submits a short update to the approving committee, co-chaired by the chief investment officer, which approves the changed terms by circulation or at its next meeting, or withdraws approval.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy: re-approval of material changes

evidence.note: Committee structure from mgr_ar21; times tier C.

steps.name: Confirm the fund documents negotiated under the commitment
steps.description: For a fund commitment whose partnership agreement and side letter were negotiated during the commitment process, counsel compares the general partner's execution versions with the agreed text and confirms the committee conditions are reflected.

error.defect_description: A late change in the execution version is not spotted.

evidence.note: Hand-off from fund-commitment, which negotiates the partnership agreement and side letter; times tier C.

steps.name: Prepare execution versions and signature packets
steps.description: The paralegal prepares clean execution versions, signature pages for the model manager as agent for each client account or entity, and incumbency or authority certificates, and routes them for electronic or wet signature.

error.defect_description: Wrong entity or client account named on a signature page.

evidence.note: Common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Authorised officers sign
steps.description: Two authorised signing officers, usually the general counsel and a senior investment officer, sign the agreement after checking counsel's confirmation note; signatures are often collected electronically in the period.

control.basis: The model manager signing authority policy: two authorised signatories

evidence.note: Two-signatory authority is assumed from common signing authority policies; the model manager's is not public.

steps.name: Counterparty countersigns and delivers the executed agreement
steps.description: The general partner, sponsor, manager or dealer countersigns and returns the executed agreement; general partners often countersign side letters only at their next closing.

evidence.note: Countersignature timing varies by counterparty; one to ten days is tier C.

steps.name: Record key terms and file the agreement
steps.description: The paralegal files the executed agreement, enters key terms in the term tracker (fees, most favoured nation rights, consent and transfer rights, reporting duties, notice periods, collateral terms) and sends the agreement to the team that onboards the investment, manager or counterparty.

error.defect_description: A reporting or consent obligation is not entered in the tracker.

next.condition: side letter with most favoured nation election to follow
deal or fund document, goes to closing
external manager agreement, goes to manager onboarding
derivative, clearing or broker agreement, goes to counterparty onboarding

evidence.note: The organisation file's process description says key terms such as fees, most favoured nation rights and consents are tracked in the document system; times tier C.

steps.name: Review the most favoured nation disclosure and elect terms
steps.description: After the fund's final closing the general partner sends the compendium of other investors' side letter terms; counsel reviews which provisions the model manager may elect, consults the deal team and returns the election form before the deadline.

next.condition: deal or fund document, goes to closing
external manager agreement, goes to manager onboarding
derivative, clearing or broker agreement, goes to counterparty onboarding

evidence.note: Equal treatment of limited partners underlies MFN rights; the timing after final close is tier C.

steps.name: Review the outside counsel invoice against the estimate
steps.description: Counsel checks the outside firm's invoice against the engagement estimate and the work done, queries overruns, approves it for payment and closes the matter.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority: budget holder approval of outside counsel invoices

next.condition: deal or fund document, goes to closing
external manager agreement, goes to manager onboarding
derivative, clearing or broker agreement, goes to counterparty onboarding

evidence.note: Invoice approval against estimates is common practice; law firms bill monthly after the work, so the wait is tier C.

exceptions.name: Extra drafting rounds
exceptions.description: The counterparty rejects key points and the draft goes through a third or fourth turn.

exceptions.name: Non-standard position escalated
exceptions.description: The other side will not move on indemnity, governing law, public body protections or confidentiality and the general counsel decides.

exceptions.name: Material change re-approved
exceptions.description: Negotiated terms move outside the committee approval and the committee re-approves or withdraws.

exceptions.name: Most favoured nation election
exceptions.description: After a fund's final closing counsel reviews other investors' side letter terms and elects those available.

exceptions.name: Negotiation abandoned
exceptions.description: The deal is lost, the sponsor moves on, the manager or dealer will not agree terms, or approval is withdrawn.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from legal instruction to executed agreement with key terms recorded
benchmarks.population: Negotiated investment agreements at a Canadian public asset manager (author's estimate)

evidence.note: Moderate-risk negotiated agreements take one to two months and high-risk ones three to four (utsa_cycle); median 40 days from negotiation to signed supplier contract (gcai_cycle, APQC); complex master agreements average 50 days (ironclad_cycle). Investment agreements mix quick amendments with long ISDA and partnership negotiations.

benchmarks.unit: CAD billion average notional of non-centrally cleared derivatives

pain_points.description: Most time is spent waiting for the other side's turn of the draft, especially general partners collecting comments from many investors and dealers queuing documentation.
Business, tax, compliance and risk input is collected one reviewer at a time by email, adding days per round.

evidence.note: Secondary reviews and internal approvals lengthen cycle times.

pain_points.description: Key terms such as most favoured nation rights, consents and reporting duties live in a spreadsheet tracker, so obligations are missed or rechecked by hand.

evidence.note: The organisation file says key terms are tracked in the document system; reliance on a spreadsheet is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Initial margin rules phased in during 2021 and 2022 added custody and credit support documentation to every new derivative counterparty.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: The model manager manages each member's assets under an investment management agreement (IMA); board-approved policies must prevent investments that contravene the restrictions set out in the IMAs, provide due diligence on sub-advisers and on custodians and brokers before they hold assets, and keep books and records of transactions for members.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Management Investment Committee with the General Counsel; three Investment Department Committees with Legal representatives approve decisions up to thresholds; eight new private equity co-investments or direct deals and two follow-ons in 2021; the model manager reduced external managers and added strategic partners.

sources.title: The model manager posts 2021 net return of 9.6%, outperforms benchmark (news release, 25 April 2022)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: 35 direct and co-investment transactions in 2021; four private equity fund commitments; new strategic partner commitments named.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0: fund governance (fiduciary duties, exculpation and indemnification, conflicts, equal treatment)
sources.supports: Limited partners should reject partnership agreement terms that dilute fiduciary duties; minimum exculpation standard; indemnification expenses capped; no conflicted actions without prior written advisory committee approval; arrangements with some investors should not disadvantage others.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0: GP-led secondary transactions
sources.supports: GP-led transactions need advisory committee approval of conflicts, disclosure of bids and terms, sufficient time for limited partners to evaluate and elect, and a status quo option.

sources.title: ILPA templates, standards and model documents
sources.supports: ILPA publishes a model limited partnership agreement, a model non-disclosure agreement and a model subscription agreement (December 2017) for negotiating fund terms.

sources.title: Guideline E-22: Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
sources.supports: Initial margin phase-in: groups above $75 billion average notional from 1 September 2021 and above $12 billion from 1 September 2022; initial margin methodology and dispute procedures agreed before trading; initial margin held so the poster is protected; written netting contracts with legal review.

sources.title: Cycle times and contract timeframes
sources.publisher: University of Texas at San Antonio, Business Contracts Office
sources.supports: Negotiated agreements: low risk 10 to 14 business days, moderate risk one to two months, high risk three to four months to full execution; after first review, timing depends on the other party's flexibility and response time, secondary reviews and internal approvals.

sources.title: Contract cycle time: benchmarks and how to measure it
sources.supports: APQC benchmarks reported: median legal contract review of 15 days across 69 companies (receipt to turnaround) and median of 40 calendar days across 3,081 companies from opening negotiation to a signed supplier contract.

sources.title: How to slash contract cycle time
sources.supports: Citing a 2025 contracting benchmark report: a simple NDA averages 5 days and a complex master agreement 50 days in technology companies; custom agreements take weeks to months.

sources.title: Summary: Legal Counsel (NOC 41101) near Toronto (ON)
sources.supports: Median wage $69.74 an hour for NOC 41101 in the Toronto region; fair job prospects.

assumptions: Mix of agreements (tier C): deal and fund documents and their consents about 50%, external manager agreements 17%, derivative, clearing and broker agreements 13%, other amendments, consents and waivers 20%. The END outcomes are drawn in these proportions because the step graph does not remember the agreement type.

Fund partnership agreements and side letters are negotiated inside fund-commitment (its steps s22 to s25); here those cases (10%) only confirm execution versions, sign and record terms, so negotiation time is not counted twice.
principal_private_equity stands in for all private market principals, and pm_global_credit for all portfolio managers who own external mandates; their FTE covers those peers.
Outside law firm hours are not modelled as roles; outside counsel is used on about 30% of matters, shown as the engagement step, waits and in-house review time.

The general partner's or dealer's paper is the starting point for most agreements; the model manager-form manager agreements start with outside counsel or the manager's first mark-up, which is modelled as the same external wait.
Two authorised signatories are assumed; the model manager's signing authority policy is not public.

tax_manager, compliance_analyst, investment_risk_manager, principal_private_equity, pm_global_credit, tpm_portfolio_manager and cio are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading). Hands-on time of about 24 hours per agreement across in-house roles (about 18 for counsel) is the author's estimate. The simulated 90th percentile (about 68 days) is below the 110-day estimate because long ISDA and partnership negotiations are a small share of cases.
Web searching ran out while this workflow was researched, so sources were limited to pages fetched by address; several step times and rates remain tier C.
